chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, may Allah be pleased with him, told us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar told us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:
The avaricious is only the one who prevented the right of Allah and spent in other than the right of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He.

key_terms.حَقَّ اللَّهِ: The right of Allah (obligatory spending like khums, zakat, or charity)
key_terms.غَيْرِ حَقِّ اللَّهِ: Other than the right of Allah (spending on permissible but non-obligatory or wasteful things)

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of stinginess in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) via the chain of Zurara, redefining stinginess (*shah*) as a spiritual misallocation of resources rather than mere hoarding. This view emphasizes that true avarice lies in neglecting obligatory dues (*haqq Allah*) while squandering wealth on non-divine pursuits, linking economic discipline directly to theological accountability.

en.basel-kadem: 5.	We were told by Muhammed bin Hasan bin Ahmad bin Waleed, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: We were told by Muhammed bin Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad bin Muhammed, from his father, from Hammad bin Isa, from Huraiz, from Zurara, that he said: I heard Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, say:
The avaricious is only the one who prevented the right of Allah and spent in other than the right of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He.
